messages:
Kevin (Client SDK): Hey team — Acme ran a reconciliation and says the invoice token total is ~30% higher than what our JS SDK estimator reported. They attached a curl + SDK logs. Can someone help triage?

Aj (Billing): Which account and invoice? I can pull the raw usage if we have ids.

Kevin (Client SDK): acct_ABC123, invoice inv_2026-03-01. They included the API response usage block from our hosted endpoint: 
```json
{
  \"id\": \"resp_01\",
  \"usage\": { \"prompt_tokens\": 2100, \"completion_tokens\": 1200, \"total_tokens\": 3300 }
}
```
Their SDK estimator returned ~2500 total (prompt+completion).

Maria (Support): Do they use any function/tool calls or retrievals? Tool outputs often change what gets counted depending on whether the tool reply is returned as part of completion or stitched into future prompts. Also check for hidden system messages we add server-side.

Kevin (Client SDK): They use a chat flow: system + user prompt, then model calls a tool `lookup_product` (function call) that returns a 600-token JSON snippet which we then include back into the conversation as an assistant message. The SDK estimator we ship tokenizes only the original request payload (system + user) and an estimated completion length. It does not re-tokenize the tool output after the server returns it.

Sasha (Eng-ML): Short explainer: our billing meter counts tokens on the final server-side sequence(s) used by the model. That includes: (1) the system message(s) we might inject on the server (e.g., internal safety/obfuscation text), (2) any tool/connector outputs that are appended to the conversation as assistant messages, and (3) assistant/model-generated function arguments (if present). Client-side estimators that only tokenize the initial request will often undercount.

Sasha (Eng-ML): Example repro to demonstrate the gap:
1) Send a chat completion with a system + user message and enable function calling.
2) Have the model call a function which returns a ~600-token JSON blob.
3) Server returns usage showing completion_tokens inflated because tool output was returned as an assistant message in the completion.

Kevin (Client SDK): Repro curl we used (simplified):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Lookup product 123 and summarize."}],"functions":[{"name":"lookup_product","parameters":{}}],"temperature":0}'
```
Then the server response contains the function call and our connector's payload is placed back into the assistant message. Usage block attached (prompt 2100 / completion 1200 / total 3300).

Maria (Support): Action items I suggest:
- Kevin: attach the raw HTTP response (full JSON) and the SDK estimator output (copy/paste) for the same run.
- Sasha: confirm whether we inject any internal system messages for acct_ABC123 (we have a few account-specific retrievals that can add 50-400 tokens).
- Aj: I'll hold invoice adjustments pending triage; flag opened on the account so we don't autopay disputes.

Sasha (Eng-ML): Quick note on estimator differences: our SDK estimator can be configured to re-tokenize the full end-state conversation (including assistant messages) to match server billing. We recommend clients run the estimator against the final conversation transcript (post-tool output). By default many integrations only estimate before the function output is available, causing an undercount.

Kevin (Client SDK): For reproducibility, here's the minimal client-side JS estimator snippet the customer used: 
```js
const est = estimator.tokenCount(system + user) + Math.round(estimatedCompletionTokens);
// never re-tokenizes assistant/tool return
```

meterbot: Automated flag: acct_ABC123 flagged for manual invoice review (rule: sudden >20% variance).

Maria (Support): If Kevin can drop the raw response & SDK logs here I'll attach them to the billing ticket and loop Legal if needed. Also please include whether streaming was used (streaming can slightly change how partial tokens are reported in logs).

Kevin (Client SDK): Dropping examples now (sent to #private-attachments). Streaming was off for this run.

Aj (Billing): Thanks. If we confirm server-injected messages or tool outputs are counted in the invoice, we'll propose a one-time credit and a doc update on how to align client estimators with server billing.

Sasha (Eng-ML): TL;DR: Most likely cause = tool output (assistant message) tokens + any server-side injected system context. Fix = reproduce with full transcript and re-tokenize final assistant messages, or configure SDK to include tool responses when estimating.

Maria (Support): I'll keep this thread updated after we get the raw files attached to the billing ticket. :thumbsup:
